newsitem.title: USA: Wall Street stocks higher at midday, bonds weak.
newsitem.headline: Wall Street stocks higher at midday, bonds weak.

text.p: Wall Street stocks were higher at midday but their advance was restrained by a weak bond market where investors took profits after Tuesday's rally.
The Dow Industrials were up 11 at 6018 while advances led declines by 11 to 10 on volume of about 225 million shares. The long bond was off 4/32 to yield 6.69 percent.

"The focus has shifted from earnings to the economy and interest rates, and there the news was good until the new home sales report today," said Hugh Johnson, chief investment officer at First Albany Corp.

U.S. Treasuries rallied in early trading on a preliminary estimate that GDP expanded at a 2.2 percent rate in the third quarter. That exceeded forecasts of a 1.8 percent gain but it was well below the 4.7 percent increase in the second quarter.

But the rally faltered after the release of U.S. new home sales, which fell 0.5 percent to an annualized rate of 816,000 from a revised 820,000 in August. The forecast had been for 768,000, according to a Reuter survey of U.S. economists,
"The home sales were stronger than expected and took the gusto out of the bond market, and the stock market started to stabilize," Johnson said.

Johnson said the early decline in interest rates on evidence of slowing economic growth was a mixed blessing for stocks because it suggested that corporate earnings in the fourth quarter and beyond could suffer.

"It looks as though the Federal Reserve will put policy on hold. That is a good thing. But the offset is that it may be tough to top third-quarter earnings in the quarter and after that," he said. "Stocks of retailers are doing poorly, and that is exactly what you would expect in an environment in which consumer spending is slowing. This raises real questions about earnings in general and the retailers in particular."
The immediate catalyst for the weakness in retailers was a sector downgrade from Goldman Sachs.

The brokerage said it lowered its ratings on Wal-Mart Stores Inc and Gymboree Corp to market perform from recommended, and its ratings on Dillard Department Stores Inc and TJX Cos Inc to market perform from outperform. Wal-Mart was down one at 26-3/8, Gymboree fell 2-1/8 to 31-1/8, Dillard fell one to 30-3/4 and TJX fell 1-7/8 to 39-3/8.
Another unsettling factor is the prospect of Democrats taking over the House of Representatives on November 5.

"The general consenus is that such a result would not be good for the bond market," Johnson said. He said that while President Clinton had moved to cut the deficit, an even deeper cut would involve slashing entitlements, something the president has been reluctant to undertake.
"If the Democrats win the House they will support Clinton's reluctance," Johnson said.
Among special situations, Nuco2 Inc (Fowler Carbonics Inc) was down 5-1/4 at 13-3/4 after Raymond James lowered its rating on the stock to accumulate from buy.
Elsag Bailey Process Automations NV was down six at 16-5/8 on the NYSE after a delayed opening, as analysts downgraded the stock amid concerns over bookings.

CompUSA Inc was down 5-3/4 at 45-3/4 after Chief Executive Officer Jim Halpin said the company's retail sales had been "somewhat sluggish" and that he was looking ahead to the holiday selling season with only "cautious optimism."
